51.solution: KCN is the salt of a strong base \((\text{KOH})\) and a weak acid \((\text{HCN})\).\nThe \(\text{CN}^-\) anion undergoes hydrolysis, making the solution basic.\n\(\text{NaNO}_3\) is a salt of strong acid and strong base (neutral); \(\text{CH}_3\text{COONH}_4\) and \(\text{NH}_4\text{F}\) are weak-acid/weak-base salts (near neutral / depends).

52.solution: 2-Bromobutane with aqueous NaOH undergoes nucleophilic substitution (\(\text{OH}^-\) replaces Br).\n\(\text{CH}_3\text{-CHBr-CH}_2\text{-CH}_3 + \text{NaOH}_{(aq)} \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{-CH(OH)-CH}_2\text{-CH}_3 + \text{NaBr}\)\nProduct is butan-2-ol. (Alcoholic KOH would give elimination instead.)

53.solution: Reduction: \(\text{Mn}^{+7}(\text{KMnO}_4) \rightarrow \text{Mn}^{+2}(\text{MnSO}_4)\), a 5-electron change.\n\(\text{Mn}^{+7} + 5e^- \rightarrow \text{Mn}^{+2}\): 5 F per mole.\nFor 2 mol: \(2 \times 5 = 10\) F.

54.solution: Moles of \(\text{N}_2 = \dfrac{56}{28} = 2\) mol.\nAt STP, 1 mol occupies \(22.4\) L.\n\(V = 2 \times 22.4 = 44.8\) L.

55.subtopic: First Law of Thermodynamics, Internal Energy and Work

56.subtopic: Rate of Reaction, Stoichiometry and Average Rate
56.solution:
Rate \(= -\dfrac{1}{2}\dfrac{d[x]}{dt} = -\dfrac{d[y]}{dt} = +\dfrac{1}{2}\dfrac{d[z]}{dt}\).
Negative sign \(\Rightarrow\) x and y are reactants; positive \(\Rightarrow\) z is product.
Stoichiometric coefficients from the reciprocals: x = 2, y = 1, z = 2.
Reaction: \(2x + y ightarrow 2z\).

57.solution: Relative lowering \(\dfrac{\Delta P}{P_1^0} = 0.018\), \(P_1^0 = 18\) mm Hg.\n\(\Delta P = 0.018 \times 18 = 0.324\) mm Hg.\n\(P_1 = P_1^0 - \Delta P = 18 - 0.324 = 17.68\) mm Hg.

58.subtopic: Colour, Magnetic Properties and Spin-Only Formula
58.solution: Spin-only moment \(\mu = \sqrt{n(n+2)}\) BM increases with unpaired electrons n.\n\(\text{Mn}^{2+}\) (\(3d^5\)): n = 5; \(\text{Ti}^{3+}\) (\(3d^1\)): n = 1; \(\text{Cu}^{2+}\) (\(3d^9\)): n = 1; \(\text{Ni}^{2+}\) (\(3d^8\)): n = 2.\n\(\text{Mn}^{2+}\) has the most unpaired electrons, hence highest moment.

59.solution: Polyacrylonitrile (Orlon/Acrilan) is used as a wool substitute (synthetic fibre).\nGlyptal is a paint/coating resin, Terylene is a polyester fibre, Neoprene is a synthetic rubber.

60.subtopic: IUPAC Nomenclature, Functional Groups and Homologous Series
60.solution: Thiophene is a five-membered ring with sulphur (no nitrogen).\nPyridine, pyrrole and piperidine all contain nitrogen.

61.subtopic: Real Gases, Dalton's Law and KTG
61.solution:
For equal partial pressures at the same T and V, equal moles are needed: \(n_{Ne} = n_{He}\).
\(n_{He} = \dfrac{4}{4} = 1\) mol.
\(n_{Ne} = 1 = \dfrac{m_{Ne}}{20} \Rightarrow m_{Ne} = 20\) g.
Wait \(-\) recheck: mass of Ne \(= 1 	imes 20 = 20\) g... however the AK keys 4 g. Re-examine below.
61.note: Independent derivation: equal partial pressure at same V,T requires equal moles. n(He)=4/4=1 mol, so n(Ne) must =1 mol, giving m(Ne)=1*20=20 g (option D). The AK keys A (4 g), and even the AK's own worked solution derives m(Ne)=20 g, contradicting its keyed letter. Correct answer is D (20 g).

62.subtopic: Bonding Theories, EAN, Crystal Field, Hybridization and Magnetism
62.solution: EAN = (atomic no. of metal) \(-\) (oxidation state) + 2\(\times\)(no. of ligands).\nZn: Z = 30, oxidation state +2, 4 \(\text{NH}_3\) ligands donating 2e\(^-\) each.\nEAN \(= 30 - 2 + (4 \times 2) = 30 - 2 + 8 = 36\).

63.subtopic: Galvanic Cells, EMF, Nernst Equation and Thermodynamics
63.solution: Spontaneous if \(E^0_{cell} = E^0_{cathode} - E^0_{anode} > 0\).\n(C) Zn + Cu\(^{2+}\): cathode Cu (+0.34), anode Zn (\(-0.76\)): \(E^0 = 0.34 - (-0.76) = +1.1\) V \(> 0\).\nAll other options give negative \(E^0_{cell}\).

64.subtopic: Physical Properties of Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers
64.solution: Pure phenol is a colourless (often pinkish on standing), toxic, low-melting solid with a characteristic carbolic odour.\nThe statement "odourless, nontoxic, high melting solid" is FALSE \(\Rightarrow\) option B is the NOT-true statement.

65.subtopic: IUPAC and Common Nomenclature of Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers
65.solution: sec-Butyl alcohol is \(\text{CH}_3\text{-CH(OH)-CH}_2\text{-CH}_3\); the carbinol (C-OH) carbon bears a methyl and an ethyl group.\nIn the carbinol system, groups are named alphabetically + "carbinol": ethyl methyl carbinol.

66.stemOverride: Calculate the number of unit cells in \(1\,\text{cm}^3\) volume of metal if unit cell edge length is \(1.25 \times 10^{-8}\,\text{cm}\).
66.note: Stem dropped the leading digit of edge length; AK solution uses 1.25e-8 cm which gives 5.12e23. stemOverride restores it.

67.solution: \(\Delta T_b = K_b \cdot m = K_b \cdot \dfrac{n_{solute}}{\text{kg solvent}}\).\n\(0.8 = 2 \times \dfrac{n}{0.5}\).\n\(n = \dfrac{0.8 \times 0.5}{2} = 0.2\) mol.

68.solution: Temperature is a state function (path-independent) and an intensive property (independent of amount).\nInternal energy and entropy are extensive; volume is extensive.

69.solution: Reduction of nitrile (Mendius reaction): \(\text{CH}_3\text{-C}\equiv\text{N} + 4[\text{H}] \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{-CH}_2\text{-NH}_2\).\nFour H atoms are required for complete reduction of one mole of acetonitrile to ethylamine.

70.subtopic: pH, pOH and Ionic Product of Water

71.solution: A + lithium amide \(\rightarrow\) ethynyl lithium \(\rightarrow\) (with bromoethane) but-1-yne.\nEthyne (\(\text{HC}\equiv\text{CH}\)) is deprotonated by \(\text{LiNH}_2\) to ethynyl lithium (\(\text{HC}\equiv\text{C-Li}\)).\nSo A = ethyne.

72.subtopic: Molar Conductivity, Kohlrausch's Law and Degree of Dissociation

73.solution: 2-chloro-2-methylbutane: C2 is bonded to \(\text{Cl}\), two \(\text{CH}_3\) groups and an ethyl group \(-\) two identical substituents \(\Rightarrow\) achiral, optically inactive.\nThe others (3-chlorohexane, 2-chloropentane, 2-chloro-3-methylbutane) have a chiral carbon \(\Rightarrow\) optically active.

74.solution: Picric acid (2,4,6-trinitrophenol) is made by nitrating phenol with conc. \(\text{HNO}_3\) + conc. \(\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4\), which generates the strong electrophile \(\text{NO}_2^+\).

75.subtopic: Rate Law, Order, Molecularity and Rate Expression
75.solution: \(\text{H}_2 + \text{I}_2 \rightarrow 2\text{HI}\) is a classic bimolecular, second-order reaction (rate \(= k[\text{H}_2][\text{I}_2]\)).\nDecomposition of \(\text{H}_2\text{O}_2\) and of \(\text{CH}_3\text{CHO}\) are first order; the NO + H\(_2\) reaction is third order.

76.solution: Packing efficiency of fcc = 74%.\nVolume occupied by particles \(= 0.74 \times V_{cell} = 0.74 \times 6.4 \times 10^{-23}\).\n\(= 4.736 \times 10^{-23}\,\text{cm}^3\).

77.subtopic: Carboxylic Acids, Properties, Reactions and Derivatives
77.solution: Acid anhydrides hydrolyse to carboxylic acids.\n\((\text{CH}_3\text{CO})_2\text{O} + \text{H}_2\text{O} \rightarrow 2\,\text{CH}_3\text{COOH}\) (acetic acid).

78.subtopic: Glycosidic Linkages in Di- and Polysaccharides
78.solution: Amylose is a linear polymer of glucose joined only by \(\alpha\text{-}1,4\) glycosidic linkages.\n(Amylopectin has both \(\alpha\text{-}1,4\) and \(\alpha\text{-}1,6\) linkages.)

79.subtopic: Dipole Moment, Polarity and Intermolecular Forces
79.solution: Resultant dipole moments: \(\text{H}_2\text{S} \approx 0.95\) D, \(\text{NH}_3 \approx 1.47\) D, \(\text{NF}_3 \approx 0.23\) D, \(\text{CHCl}_3 \approx 1.04\) D.\n\(\text{NH}_3\) has the largest dipole moment (lone pair and bond dipoles add), hence most polar.

80.subtopic: Reactions of Alkenes, Addition, Oxidation and Ozonolysis
80.solution: 2-methylbut-2-ene \(\text{(CH}_3)_2\text{C=CH-CH}_3\) + HCl: Markovnikov addition puts \(\text{H}\) on the less-substituted carbon and \(\text{Cl}\) on the more-substituted (3\(^\circ\)) carbon.\nMajor product: 2-chloro-2-methylbutane.

81.subtopic: Group 2 Alkaline Earth Metals, Properties and Reactivity
81.solution: Alkaline earth metals dissolve in liquid ammonia giving deep blue-black coloured solutions (due to ammoniated electrons), similar to alkali metals.

82.solution: Drinking straws are made of polypropylene (PP) \(-\) rigid, lightweight and heat-resistant.

83.subtopic: First-Order Kinetics, Rate Constant and Half-Life

84.subtopic: Side-Chain Reactions, Oxidation and Other Transformations
84.solution: Ethylbenzene with (i) alk. \(\text{KMnO}_4\) (ii) \(\text{H}_3\text{O}^+\): the entire alkyl side chain is oxidised to a single \(\text{-COOH}\) attached to the ring.\nProduct: benzoic acid, \(\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{-COOH}\).

85.solution: Osmotic pressure \(\propto\) number of particles (i factor) for equimolar solutions.\nKCl \(\rightarrow\) 2; \(\text{BaCl}_2 \rightarrow\) 3; \(\text{AlCl}_3 \rightarrow\) 4; \(\text{Al}_2(\text{SO}_4)_3 \rightarrow\) 5.\nIncreasing order: \(\text{KCl} < \text{BaCl}_2 < \text{AlCl}_3 < \text{Al}_2(\text{SO}_4)_3\).

86.subtopic: Green Chemistry, Principles, Atom Economy and Green Solvents
86.solution: Clove yields eugenol, which is useful for extracting analgesic and antimicrobial compounds.

87.subtopic: Inner Transition Elements, Lanthanoids and Actinoids
87.solution: Across the lanthanoid series, ionic radius decreases (lanthanide contraction) from \(\text{La}^{3+}\) to \(\text{Lu}^{3+}\).\nLu lies at the end, so \(\text{Lu}^{3+}\) has the smallest +3 ionic size.

88.solution: Nylon 2-nylon 6 is a biodegradable polyamide made from glycine (\(\text{H}_2\text{N-CH}_2\text{-COOH}\)) and \(\varepsilon\)-amino caproic acid.

89.subtopic: Bonding Theories, EAN, Crystal Field, Hybridization and Magnetism
89.solution: Spectrochemical series (increasing field strength): \(\text{I}^- < \text{Br}^- < \text{Cl}^- < \text{S}^{2-} < \text{F}^- < \text{OH}^- < \ldots\)\nAmong the listed ligands the increasing order is \(\text{I}^- < \text{Cl}^- < \text{S}^{2-} < \text{OH}^-\).
89.note: No AK extracted. Derived independently from the spectrochemical series: I- < Cl- < S2- < OH- (option B). Confident.

90.subtopic: Ionic Equilibrium, Ka, Kb and Degree of Dissociation

91.solution: Lone pairs on the central atom:\n\(\text{BrF}_5\): 1; \(\text{XeF}_6\): 1; ICl: 3; \(\text{H}_2\text{S}\): 2; \(\text{ClF}_3\): 2; \(\text{XeF}_2\): 3; \(\text{IF}_7\): 0; \(\text{XeF}_4\): 2.\nThe pair with equal lone pairs (1 each) is \(\text{BrF}_5\) and \(\text{XeF}_6\).

92.solution: \(\text{N}_2\text{O}_5\) is the anhydride of \(\text{HNO}_3\), an acidic oxide.\nCO, NO and \(\text{N}_2\text{O}\) are neutral oxides.

93.solution: Let oxidation number of S = x in \(\text{SO}_3\): \(x + 3(-2) = 0 \Rightarrow x = +6\).

94.subtopic: Colloids, Classification, Coagulation and Hardy-Schulze Rule
94.solution: Macromolecular colloids consist of large molecules: e.g. nylon, starch, cellulose, proteins.\n\(\text{S}_8\) is a multimolecular colloid; soap and detergent are associated colloids.

95.subtopic: Unit Cells, Edge Length and Atomic Radius
95.solution: A corner particle in any cubic unit cell is shared among 8 adjacent unit cells (contribution 1/8 each).

96.subtopic: Preparation Methods of Aldehydes and Ketones
96.solution: Etard reaction: toluene is oxidised by chromyl chloride (\(\text{CrO}_2\text{Cl}_2\)) to a chromium complex, which on hydrolysis gives benzaldehyde.

97.solution: At equilibrium \(\Delta G = 0\): \(T = \dfrac{\Delta H}{\Delta S}\).\n\(T = \dfrac{-210000\,\text{J}}{-150\,\text{J K}^{-1}} = 1400\) K.

98.solution: Unpaired electrons: F (\(2p^5\)) = 1; Na (\(3s^1\)) = 1; N (\(2p^3\)) = 3; O (\(2p^4\)) = 2.\nNitrogen has the maximum (3) unpaired electrons.

99.subtopic: Chemical Reactions and Basicity of Amines
99.solution: The carbylamine (isocyanide) test gives a foul smell only with PRIMARY amines (\(\text{R-NH}_2\)) on heating with \(\text{CHCl}_3\) + ethanolic KOH.\nAmong the options only \(\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{NH}_2\) is a primary amine; the others are secondary/tertiary.
99.note: Carbylamine test is positive only for PRIMARY amines. Option D (CH3CH2NH2, ethylamine) is the only primary amine; option B ((CH3)2NH, dimethylamine) is secondary and gives NO foul smell. AK keys B which is wrong. Correct answer is D.

100.subtopic: Nucleic Acids, DNA, RNA, Nucleotides and Bases
100.solution: The sugar in an RNA nucleotide is D-ribose, a pentose with 5 carbon atoms.
